summary: Erdosteine is a thiol-containing mucolytic with antioxidant properties used as adjunct therapy in respiratory disorders with excessive or viscid mucus, including acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis/COPD. The usual adult dose is 300 mg twice daily for up to about 10 days. Its active metabolite breaks disulphide bonds in mucus, reducing sputum viscosity and improving clearance, and it also protects against oxidant-mediated airway damage.
indications: Symptomatic treatment of acute and chronic respiratory disorders associated with excessive, thick or viscid mucus (mucolytic)
Adjunct in acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis / COPD with productive cough

dosage.n: Short course, generally up to 10 days

dosage.d: Up to 600 mg twice daily per local label

admin: Granules/sachets where available are dispersed in water and taken immediately
Can be taken with or without food
Keep treatment short (typically up to 10 days unless directed)
Increase fluid intake to aid sputum clearance
moa: Erdosteine is a prodrug; its active thiol-containing metabolite (Met 1) opens the disulphide bonds linking glycoprotein fibres in mucus, reducing sputum viscosity and elasticity and improving mucociliary clearance. The free sulfhydryl groups also scavenge reactive oxygen species and protect alpha-1 antitrypsin from oxidative inactivation, and erdosteine has been shown to reduce bacterial adhesion to respiratory epithelium.

absolute: Homocystinuria (contains a sulphur amino acid analogue)
monitor: Persistent or worsening cough beyond expected course

preg: There are insufficient data on use in pregnant women; as a precaution erdosteine is not recommended during pregnancy and should be avoided unless clearly necessary.
lact: It is unknown whether erdosteine or its metabolites are excreted in human milk; use during breastfeeding is not recommended.
renal: Contraindicated when creatinine clearance is below 25 mL/min because the active metabolite may accumulate; use with caution in lesser degrees of impairment.
hepatic: In mild to moderate hepatic impairment the daily dose should not exceed 300 mg; erdosteine should be avoided in severe hepatic impairment.

moderate: Antitussives (e.g. codeine, dextromethorphan) - suppressing cough while liquefying secretions can cause mucus retention; avoid combining
minor: Theoretically may enhance the antibacterial effect of co-administered amoxicillin in airway secretions (described in studies)
interactions.food: No clinically significant food interaction; can be taken with meals.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction reported; moderate alcohol intake.

monitoring: Clinical response - reduction in sputum viscosity and improved cough clearance
Reassess if cough persists beyond the expected treatment course

counsel: Take as a short course exactly as directed; do not exceed the recommended dose
Drink plenty of fluids to help loosen and clear mucus
Do not combine with a cough suppressant unless your doctor advises
Stop and seek help if you develop rash, facial swelling or difficulty breathing
pk: Mucolytic effect within hours of dosing
Store below 25-30 C, protect from moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved; record based on EMA/SmPC and BNF-type sources, pending clinical review. Marketed in Europe and Asia (e.g. Italy, UK, India).
Prodrug - activity comes from the thiol metabolite that cleaves mucus disulphide bonds, similar in concept to acetylcysteine but better tolerated gastrically
Contains a sulphur amino acid moiety - contraindicated in homocystinuria and avoid in active peptic ulcer
Antioxidant action protects alpha-1 antitrypsin from oxidant inactivation, of interest in COPD
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not double up. As this is usually a short course, resume the normal twice-daily schedule.
overdose: Overdose experience is limited; expect exaggerated gastrointestinal effects (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain). Management is symptomatic and supportive; there is no specific antidote.
